# HDialog

> A native modal dialog with focus containment, Escape dismissal, and focus return. Keep it inside your theme island.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.5.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HDialog` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-dialog>`.
- Constructor: `HearthDialogElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Feedback.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HDialog.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Use the open prop/property; do not set a native open attribute on an inner dialog or call showModal() yourself.
- Handle close() by setting open=false. Native dialog supplies modal focus behavior, Escape dismissal, and focus return.
- Keep the component inside its theme island. The native top layer removes the need to teleport the component away from inherited tokens.

## Public API

open: boolean · title: string · description: string

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    open?: boolean;
    title: string;
    description?: string;
};
```

### Defaults

No component defaults; optional props are undefined (absent boolean props cast to false unless explicitly defaulted).

### Events

close() — set open=false in your handler

```ts
type Emits = {
    close: [
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

default, footer

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

dialog, header, body

Use `hearth-dialog::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { HDialog, HButton, HInput } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';
const open = ref(false);
</script>

<template>
  <HButton @click="open = true">Edit workspace</HButton>
  <HDialog :open="open" title="Workspace details" @close="open = false">
    <HInput label="Workspace name" />
    <template #footer><HButton @click="open = false">Done</HButton></template>
  </HDialog>
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-dialog');
Object.assign(element, {
  "title": "Workspace details"
});

element.innerHTML = "<hearth-input label=\"Workspace name\"></hearth-input>"; // Static example markup only; never inject untrusted HTML.

element.addEventListener('close', () => { element.open = false; });
const trigger = document.createElement('button');
trigger.textContent = 'Edit workspace';
trigger.addEventListener('click', () => { element.open = true; });
mount.before(trigger);

mount.append(element);
```

## Related components

- [HButtonBar](../button-bar/llms.txt): Group actions without changing native button focus or submission behavior.
- [HInput](../input/llms.txt): A labeled input with help/error text and native validation. Web components participate in their owning form.
- [HAlert](../alert/llms.txt): Inline feedback for success, information, and problems. Errors announce as alerts; other tones use status.
